teams.heading: Fiji chairman says Jake White won't coach flair out of side
teams.body: Fiji's chairman says Jake White will not coach the flair out of the side as the team chase a place at the 2027 World Cup. The message matters because results have been hard to find: the log shows Fiji still without a win from three matches, and their latest outing was a 15-20 loss to Japan in the Pacific Nations Cup. Next up is France in Round 4.

lead.why: It is the most-covered Fiji story in today's pack, and it is a fresh angle on the coaching change rather than a retelling of the Nawaqanitawase item already run.

teams.heading: Emmanuel Iyogun credits Ox Nche chat for path to England cap
teams.body: Northampton loosehead Emmanuel Iyogun says an out-of-the-blue message to Springbok prop Ox Nche two summers ago set him on the road to England. Nche replied politely, and the pair spent about three hours over diet Cokes talking scrums. "He had no reason to have time for me," Iyogun says. The 25-year-old made his Test debut away to Argentina in July, and credits Nche's advice on set-piece play and life for speeding his progress.

lead.why: A new men's England story about a current senior cap, and the strongest men's national-side item in the pack that is not a repeat of the Itoje story or a pundit column.

teams.heading: Ramos, Jalibert and Meafou ruled out of France's Springboks test
teams.body: Thomas Ramos, Matthieu Jalibert and Emmanuel Meafou are all out for the whole Nations Championship, leaving Fabien Galthié to rebuild France's side for the Springboks test in Paris. Planet Rugby's view is that the losses are about quality rather than depth: Jalibert is described as the best attacking ten in the Northern Hemisphere over four seasons, and Meafou as scrum ballast nobody else in France can provide. Julien Marchand and Régis Montagne are doubtful, and Thibaud Flament, Demba Bamba and Lenni Nouchi are also out.

lead.why: Candidates 1 and 2 repeat the squad story already run today, while this is a new injury story with a clear France angle ahead of the Springboks test.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan named Ireland captain again as Caelan Doris misses November
teams.body: Dan Sheehan will once again captain Ireland through the four-game November window, with Caelan Doris ruled out by injury. Hooker Sheehan takes the armband in Doris's absence from a squad already shorn of several key men: Jack Crowley, Harry Byrne and Bryn Ward are also out. Jack Conan, who hurt a shoulder in Leinster's 48-23 win at Clermont Auvergne last weekend, will miss the window too.

lead.why: It is a new item about the men's squad that is distinct from the call-ups already run, and it puts a named Ireland player at the centre of the story.

teams.heading: Italy reported to be missing 12 players for next month's Nations Championship
teams.body: Italy are reported to be missing 12 players for next month's Nations Championship, a number that would test Gonzalo Quesada's depth before a busy November. Fixtures take them to Turin to face South Africa, then Genoa against Argentina and Udine against Fiji, before the finals at Twickenham. Toulouse centre Tommaso Menoncello is one name already set to miss, with a shoulder sprain expected to keep him out for several weeks.

lead.why: It is the biggest new squad story for the national side, and it is not the Menoncello injury already reported.

teams.heading: Scotland's first All Blacks game in New Zealand in 27 years confirmed
teams.body: Scotland will face the All Blacks in New Zealand for the first time in 27 years, a separate trip from their Round 4 meeting with the same side. Their last outing was a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round 3, and they have won two of three so far, sitting fifth of 12 in the log.

teams.heading: Lyn Jones tips Scarlets wing Macs Page for 'huge future' with Wales
teams.body: Former Dragons and Ospreys boss Lyn Jones says Scarlets wing Macs Page has a "huge future" with Wales, despite his omission from Steve Tandy's Nations Championship squad. Jones, speaking to BBC Radio Wales, feels Page's age may have counted against him, and calls him "one of the best players I have seen playing this season". Page, 21, toured Japan with Wales in 2025 without winning a cap, and RUCK reports four tries in four Scarlets appearances so far.

lead.why: It is the newest item in the pack, and it gives the reader a fresh angle on the squad omissions without repeating the squad announcement.

teams.heading: Argentina's best-ever world ranking is No. 3, reached in 2007–08
teams.body: Argentina's best-ever world ranking is No. 3, reached in 2007–08. Set against that high-water mark, the current log has them eighth of 12, with one win and two defeats from three matches and a 28-28 draw with Australia as their most recent result. Across those three matches they have scored 97 and conceded 99. Their next fixture is Round 4 against Ireland.

teams.heading: Isuzu named official automotive partner for Australia's 2027 men's World Cup
teams.body: World Rugby has confirmed Isuzu Motors as Official Automotive Partner for the men's World Cup in Australia in 2027 and the Women's World Cup in 2029. For Wallabies fans, the sponsor adds a visible layer to a home tournament, with Isuzu committing to fan-led activations at venues and Fan Festivals across the host cities. Isuzu, which has more than 160 authorised outlets across Australia, is also exploring transport solutions for participating teams and the tournament workforce.

lead.why: The only genuinely new item that is not a retelling of the Genia piece already run today.

teams.heading: Japan men's sevens beat Hong Kong China 28-14 in Asia series final
teams.body: Japan's men's sevens side got some revenge on Hong Kong China, winning 28-14 in the final of Leg 2 of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series in Colombo. The result inflicted a rare defeat on the defending champions, though Hong Kong China kept the series title on points differential. Japan Men's Sevens head coach Phil Greening said the win showed the team's ability to adapt to different situations.

teams.heading: Kieran Read expects Damian McKenzie back at full-back when Richie Mo'unga recovers
teams.body: Former All Blacks captain Kieran Read expects Damian McKenzie to move back to full-back once Richie Mo'unga recovers from a calf injury. McKenzie has started the last two Bledisloe Cup Tests at fly-half after Mo'unga and Ruben Love were ruled out. Ex-All Blacks scrum-half Justin Marshall says McKenzie has massively elevated himself, but expects the November Tests against Scotland, Wales and England to be a sterner test.

lead.why: A men's national-side selection debate that hasn't been run yet, unlike the Kirwan depth story already on the tab.

teams.heading: Cheslin Kolbe still mending jaw broken in third All Blacks Test
teams.body: Cheslin Kolbe has been mending a broken jaw since an All Blacks carrier's knee collided with it early in the third Test in Soweto, ending his game and delaying his Stormers homecoming. Speaking to former Springboks teammate Steven Kitshoff on For the Love of Rugby South Africa, Kolbe said: "It's the most frustrating injury to have." It is the second time he has broken his jaw, and he was reduced to a liquid diet. He says he is finding a positive in more time with his family.

lead.why: A new, fan-relevant update on a Springboks player's injury and recovery, which beats the pundit piece and speculative bolters lists.
